28: ## Overview
29: 
30: 
31: **mpv** is a free (as in freedom) media player for the command line. It supports
32: a wide variety of media file formats, audio and video codecs, and subtitle types.
33: 
34: There is a [FAQ][FAQ].
35: 
36: Releases can be found on the [release list][releases].
37: 
38: ## System requirements
39: 
40: - A not too ancient Linux (usually, only the latest releases of distributions
41:   are actively supported), Windows 10 1607 or later, or macOS 10.15 or later.
42: - A somewhat capable CPU. Hardware decoding might help if the CPU is too slow to
43:   decode video in realtime, but must be explicitly enabled with the `--hwdec`
44:   option.
45: - A not too crappy GPU. mpv's focus is not on power-efficient playback on
46:   embedded or integrated GPUs (for example, hardware decoding is not even
47:   enabled by default). Low power GPUs may cause issues like tearing, stutter,
48:   etc. On such GPUs, it's recommended to use `--profile=fast` for smooth playback.
49:   The main video output uses shaders for video rendering and scaling,
50:   rather than GPU fixed function hardware. On Windows, you might want to make
51:   sure the graphics drivers are current. In some cases, ancient fallback video
52:   output methods can help (such as `--vo=xv` on Linux), but this use is not
53:   recommended or supported.
54: 
55: mpv does not go out of its way to break on older hardware or old, unsupported
56: operating systems, but development is not done with them in mind. Keeping
57: compatibility with such setups is not guaranteed. If things work, consider it
58: a happy accident.
59:

83: ## Compilation
84: 
85: 
86: Compiling with full features requires development files for several
87: external libraries. Mpv requires [meson](https://mesonbuild.com/index.html)
88: to build. Meson can be obtained from your distro or PyPI.
89: 
90: After creating your build directory (e.g. `meson setup build`), you can view a list
91: of all the build options via `meson configure build`. You could also just simply
92: look at the `meson_options.txt` file. Logs are stored in `meson-logs` within
93: your build directory.
94: 
95: Example:
96: 
97:     meson setup build
98:     meson compile -C build
99:     meson install -C build
100: 
101: For libplacebo, meson can use a git check out as a subproject for a convenient
102: way to compile mpv if a sufficient libplacebo version is not easily available
103: in the build environment. It will be statically linked with mpv. Example:
104: 
105:     mkdir -p subprojects
106:     git clone https://code.videolan.org/videolan/libplacebo.git --depth=1 --recursive subprojects/libplacebo
107: 
108: Essential dependencies (incomplete list):
109: 
110: - gcc or clang
111: - X development headers (xlib, xrandr, xext, xscrnsaver, xpresent, libvdpau,
112:   libGL, GLX, EGL, xv, ...)
113: - Audio output development headers (libasound/ALSA, pulseaudio)
114: - FFmpeg libraries (libavutil libavcodec libavformat libswscale libavfilter
115:   and either libswresample or libavresample)
116: - libplacebo
117: - zlib
118: - iconv (normally provided by the system libc)
119: - libass (OSD, OSC, text subtitles)
120: - Lua (optional, required for the OSC pseudo-GUI and youtube-dl integration)
121: - libjpeg (optional, used for screenshots only)
122: - uchardet (optional, for subtitle charset detection)
123: - nvdec and vaapi libraries for hardware decoding on Linux (optional)
124: 
125: Libass dependencies (when building libass):
126: 
127: - gcc or clang, nasm on x86 and x86_64
128: - fribidi, freetype, fontconfig development headers (for libass)
129: - harfbuzz (required for correct rendering of combining characters, particularly
130:   for correct rendering of non-English text on macOS, and Arabic/Indic scripts on
131:   any platform)
132: 
133: FFmpeg dependencies (when building FFmpeg):
134: 
135: - gcc or clang, nasm on x86 and x86_64
136: - OpenSSL or GnuTLS (have to be explicitly enabled when compiling FFmpeg)
137: - libx264/libmp3lame/libfdk-aac if you want to use encoding (have to be
138:   explicitly enabled when compiling FFmpeg)
139: - For native DASH playback, FFmpeg needs to be built with --enable-libxml2
140:   (although there are security implications, and DASH support has lots of bugs).
141: - AV1 decoding support requires dav1d.
142: - For good nvidia support on Linux, make sure nv-codec-headers is installed
143:   and can be found by configure.
144: 
145: Most of the above libraries are available in suitable versions on normal
146: Linux distributions. For ease of compiling the latest git master of everything,
147: you may wish to use the separately available build wrapper ([mpv-build][mpv-build])
148: which first compiles FFmpeg libraries and libass, and then compiles the player
149: statically linked against those.
150: 
151: If you want to build a Windows binary, see [Windows compilation][windows_compilation].
152:

154: ## Release cycle
155: 
156: Once or twice a year, a release is cut off from the current development state
157: and is assigned a 0.X.0 version number. No further maintenance is done, except
158: in the event of security issues.
159: 
160: The goal of releases is to make Linux distributions happy. Linux distributions
161: are also expected to apply their own patches in case of bugs.
162: 
163: Releases other than the latest release are unsupported and unmaintained.
164: 
165: See the [release policy document][release-policy] for more information.
166: 
167: ## Bug reports
168: 
169: 
170: Please use the [issue tracker][issue-tracker] provided by GitHub to send us bug
171: reports or feature requests. Follow the template's instructions or the issue
172: will likely be ignored or closed as invalid.
173: 
174: Questions can be asked in the [discussions][discussions] or on IRC (see
175: [Contact](#Contact) below).
176: 
177: ## Contributing
178: 
179: 
180: Please read [contribute.md][contribute.md].
181: 
182: For small changes you can just send us pull requests through GitHub. For bigger
183: changes come and talk to us on IRC before you start working on them. It will
184: make code review easier for both parties later on.
185: 
186: You can check [the wiki](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/wiki/Stuff-to-do)
187: or the [issue tracker](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Ameta%3Afeature-request)
188: for ideas on what you could contribute with.
189:

195: ## History
196: 
197: This software is based on the MPlayer project. Before mpv existed as a project,

351: if not features['build-date']

355: features += {'disable-packet-pool': get_option('disable-packet-pool')}

401:

407:     flags += ['-fsanitize=address,undefined,fuzzer', '-fno-omit-frame-pointer']

457: 
458: if host_machine.system() == 'linux'
459:     sources += files('osdep/als-linux.c')

461:     sources += files('osdep/als-voctrl.c')

463:

470:

476:     'openbsd': '/dev/rcd0c',
477:     'linux': '/dev/sr0',
478: }

482:     optical_device = '/dev/cdrom'

484: 
485: features += {'android': host_machine.system() == 'android'}
